page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache, backed by instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512_VNNI) and AES-NI. The instance is configured with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is not included, meaning instances rely exclusively on external block storage services. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps, and no discrete GPUs are bundled.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily in the middle tier for parallelized and memory-centric workloads, though single-core compute performance exhibits relative limitations. Stress-ng multi-core testing yields a score of 23,622.2, Geekbench multi-core registers 8,927.0, and the PassMark CPU score reaches 23,157.62, all landing within the middle 50% band. In contrast, single-thread evaluations show weaker output, evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1,106.99, a Geekbench single-core score of 1,018.0, and poor gzip compression throughput at 19.13 GB/sec (bottom 10%). Large block memory read operations sustain 99.19 GB/sec uncached, while write bandwidth reaches 49.44 GB/sec.

From an architectural standpoint, the ecs.se1ne.8xlarge offers solid resource density for RAM-intensive deployments, but presents a performance tradeoff when tasked with single-threaded execution. With support for 22.7 million Redis SET operations per second and steady database operation benchmarks, the instance is best suited for memory-bound applications. Appropriate workload fits include in-memory databases like Redis, enterprise caching layers, large-scale relational database engines, and in-memory analytical workloads where dataset retention in RAM outweighs requirements for peak single-core CPU frequency.

Supported by AVX-512 extensions and strong multi-threaded capabilities, this server is suitable for in-memory databases, distributed caching nodes, memory-intensive data processing, and enterprise database servers requiring substantial RAM capacity.
